alternatives.description: Keep Mistral eligible while retaining the existing Anthropic and NVIDIA exclusions.
alternatives.projected_effect: Preserves one additional reviewer/provider family but conflicts with the latest explicit human vendor preference.
alternatives.risk: Garden work could continue routing to a vendor the human explicitly asked to exclude.

alternatives.description: Add Mistral AI/Mistral model and provider aliases to the existing fail-closed provider exclusion policy.
alternatives.projected_effect: Applies the same operator routing constraint uniformly without creating a new mechanism or canonical semantic rule.
alternatives.risk: Reviewer/provider diversity is reduced from the currently configured set; remaining review quorum must stay explicit.

bidirectional_gaps.gap: The current policy does not represent the latest human directive concerning Mistral.
Operational provider diversity is intentionally reduced until a future explicit human directive changes the list.

assumptions: The user explicitly directed Garden to block Mistral in addition to Anthropic and NVIDIA.
The directive is treated as a trust/procurement preference, not as proof of misconduct or model poisoning.
The existing provider exclusion owner remains the single mechanism; no parallel Mistral-specific authority or routing system is created.
Historical references may remain for audit/provenance but cannot authorize operational use.
Only a future explicit human directive may change the exclusion list.
reason.uncertainty: Aggregator and hosting metadata can change; downstream runtime guards must continue to block known Mistral model-origin/provider aliases and fail closed where an implicated identity cannot be resolved.
counterexamples: A Mistral model is selected through a third-party-hosted route.
An allowed model falls back to a Mistral provider endpoint.
A paid or free reviewer roster reintroduces Mistral after configuration drift.
An archived Mistral reference is mistaken for operational permission.
reason.conclusion: Extend the existing noncanonical fail-closed provider exclusion to Mistral, preserve factual neutrality, and require downstream routing adapters to enforce the updated list.

obligations.statement: Mistral can be added to the existing noncanonical exclusion policy without changing canonical Garden semantics or authority.
Runtime provider/model call surfaces reject Mistral model origins and provider routes.

items.claim_scope: User explicitly requested Mistral also be blocked for Garden work.
Existing machine-readable routing constraint extended with Mistral aliases and model-origin markers.
